title: Petra and the Will
premise: Jonah Vane, a concierge with an encyclopedic memory of every guest who ever passed through the Hotel Meridian, is handed a diary by a dying woman claiming her sister, Petra, vanished in 1994. The diary's final entries are dated years after Petra disappeared — written in handwriting Jonah recognizes as belonging to the hotel's beloved late owner. As Jonah traces the forged entries, he uncovers that Petra discovered the owner was embezzling from a trust meant for the hotel's long-serving staff, and she paid for it with exile, not murder: she was spirited away and paid to stay silent. The last living conspirator, now the hotel's general manager, will kill to keep it buried. In the end, Jonah chooses justice over law — exposing everything publicly rather than handing it to police bought off decades ago — and gives the recovered trust money to the staff families, finding in them the family he never had.
about_author: Petra Underhill spent fifteen years working night desks at grand old hotels before turning to writing, collecting the secrets guests leave behind like loose change. She lives above a shuttered ballroom and writes only between midnight and dawn.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Checked Out
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A frail woman named Edith checks into the Meridian after thirty years away, asks for Jonah by name, and leaves him her sister Petra's diary before dying quietly in Room 412. The final entry is dated 2001 — seven years after Petra vanished. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into professional obsession; Jonah accepts the case against his own rule about dead women.

chapters.title: Ink That Outlived Its Owner
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Forensic comparison shows the post-disappearance entries were written by Alistair Crane, the hotel's revered late owner. Jonah interviews retired staff, learning Petra was a housekeeper who 'left suddenly' in 1994. Emotional beat: disillusionment — the man everyone loved may have been the last person to betray her.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: POV alternating Jonah/Edith's letters. Jonah reconstructs the week Petra disappeared: three staff members gave identical, rehearsed statements to police. He finds the retired detective who closed the case now lives comfortably on a pension funded by the hotel. Emotional beat: creeping dread as the conspiracy reveals its scale.

chapters.title: The Trust Beneath the Floorboards
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. In the basement archives Jonah discovers the Vane Family Staff Trust — established to care for lifelong employees — drained year after year into shell accounts. Petra's job had been bookkeeping. Emotional beat: righteous anger; the theft wasn't money, it was pensions, medicine, dignity.

chapters.title: What Edith Knew
chapters.summary: POV flashback chapters via Edith's unsent letters. Edith reveals Petra found the embezzlement and confronted Alistair, who offered her silence money abroad. She took it — but kept proof. Emotional beat: moral complexity; Petra wasn't a saint, she was a survivor, and Jonah begins to love her for it.

chapters.title: The General Manager's Smile
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Current GM Marcus Hale, Alistair's protégé, realizes what Jonah is digging up. Threats arrive wrapped in courtesy: a raise, a transfer, then a photo of Jonah's estranged brother. Emotional beat: fear made personal; the case stops being academic.

chapters.title: Room 412, Again
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Searching Edith's room before it's cleared, Jonah finds Petra's hidden microfilm behind the mirror — names, dates, account numbers. Hale's men ransack the room hours later; Jonah barely escapes with the evidence. Emotional beat: adrenaline and resolve; no way back now.

chapters.title: The Night Clerk's Confession
chapters.summary: POV dual. The one conspirator still alive besides Hale — elderly night clerk Ruthie — breaks down and confesses she saw Petra put in a car in 1994 and was paid to forget. She identifies the driver: young Marcus Hale. Emotional beat: sorrow and release; witness testimony completes the paper trail.

chapters.title: Where the Law Ends
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah learns the statute of limitations has expired and the original detective will stonewall; legal justice is impossible. Hale offers him hush money and Petra's location — alive, elderly, complicit. Emotional beat: the climax of conscience; Jonah must choose exposure over the easy answer, and refuses to trade silence for truth withheld.

chapters.title: Petra and the Will
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. At the hotel's centennial gala, Jonah reads Alistair's true will aloud — a document Petra hid proving the trust's beneficiaries — and publishes everything simultaneously online. Hale is arrested on fresh fraud charges; the staff families receive their inheritance. Jonah travels to meet the aged Petra, delivering Edith's letters. Emotional beat: quiet catharsis; found family, justice outside the law, and a debt finally paid.
